item.title: Is France v South Africa on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch Springboks clash
item.description: France and South Africa clash in a mighty meeting of Test heavyweights that could prove pivotal in the Nations Championship shake-up. The Springboks are assured of a top-two finish in their pool after dismantling Italy, and will vie with New Zealand for a place in the inaugural final. The world champions face a demanding fortnight, though, with this encounter in Paris preceding a trip to Dublin to take on Ireland. Their cause is helped by an injury-hit French side facing particular questions at fly half, but Fabien Galthie’s side will be seeking a statement success having been beaten by a 14-man South Africa 12 months ago. Here’s everything you need to know. When is France vs South Africa? France vs South Africa is due to kick off at 8.10pm GMT on Friday 13 November at the Stade de France in Paris. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom can watch every game of the Nations Championship live on ITV and ITVX. Team news France are forced to install captain Antoine Dupont at fly half with all of Romain Ntamack, Matthieu Jalibert, Thomas Ramos and Antoine Hastoy absent, with Maxime Lucu partnering his skipper in the halves. Gregory Alldritt is recalled for a first international appearance in nearly a year at No 8 as Francois Cros moves to the flank. Julien Marchand is a welcome returnee at hooker as Peato Mauvaka drops to the bench. Among the replacements, a debut awaits young Pau playmaker Axel Desperes. item.title: Here's why Louisiana football's Week 11 win over ULM was its best game yet
item.description: Ahead of Louisiana football’s showdown against Louisiana-Monroe, Michael Desormeaux called the matchup his team’s biggest test of the season. It wasn’t just because the Ragin’ Cajuns were facing their cross state rivals, or because it was a Sun Belt Conference Western division matchup on the road inside St. Francis Stadium in Monroe. This game would determine the growth of this UL team at Week 11 of the college football season. The Cajuns (7-3, 4-2) showed tremendous growth as they snagged win No. 7 of the season, beating ULM 42-21 on Thursday, Nov. 12 in Monroe. The first half was nothing but a dogfight, with the Warhawks (2-8, 2-4) taking the first blow on an eight-minute touchdown drive. UL delivered the next blow, with Lunch Winfield connecting with wide receiver Shelton Sampson Jr. By the second half, the Cajuns defense took over for a half of complimentary football. Here’s why the Cajuns’ victory over their rivals was their best outing of the 2026 season. Cajuns’ defense leads to offense Knotted up 14-14 at the half, it was still anybody’s game. It had been a first half filled with adversity for the Cajuns. From allowing ULM’s quarterback Austin Carlisle to run all over them to outside linebacker Ashley Williams being carted off the field , the Cajuns had every reason to let lie down an accept defeat. UL’s defense had other plans though. To start the third quarter, safety Collin Jacob forced a fumble and linebacker Micah Johnson was right there to scoop it up and score it from 18 yards out. The Cajuns’ next score was another direct result of their defense as they forced another ULM fumble. This time, defensive lineman Maurion Eleam forced the fumble and Johnson was there again for his second fumble recovery of the night. Freshman running back JJ Garner cashed in on the turnover with a 19-yard rushing touchdown. UL would go on to score 28 points unanswered, locking in not only on defensively but offensively as well. Garner and junior running back Steven Blanco led the Cajuns’ scoring efforts with Garner rushing for 104 yards and two touchdowns on nine carries. Blanco rushed for a game-high 113 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. With only three healthy running backs remaining on the roster, the duo has been clutch in the backfield in the second half of the season. This marks the first time the Cajuns have had two running backs rush for over 100 yards in a single game since 2022. This win gives Desormeaux and his Cajuns even more momentum after becoming bowl-game eligible last week with a win over South Alabama. They will return home next week to face Coastal Carolina at 2 p.m. on Nov. 21 in the comforts of Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium. item.title: Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani’s dog ‘Decoy’ steals the show during MLB Network interview
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani’s dog ‘Decoy’ steals the show during MLB Network interview appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani ’s dog Decoy had another show-stealing performance on Thursday. As the Dodgers star was being interviewed on MLB Network ahead of the NL MVP announcement, he was petting and rubbing his trusty dog (who seemed to be wearing a green hoodie) on his lap as he answered questions. Another MVP finalist season for Shohei Ohtani means another Decoy appearance 🐶 pic.twitter.com/ftkd4k8Vr4 — MLB (@MLB) November 13, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Decoy’s appearances on the MVP announcement shows have become an annual event at this point. His first appearance came in 2023 when Ohtani was still part of the Los Angeles Angels. He made another appearance in 2024 as Shohei won the NL MVP in his first season with the Los Angeles Dodgers. Following his occasional TV appearances, Decoy has gone on to become a full-blown celebrity. The Dodgers had a Decoy bobblehead night back in 2024. Ohtani also released a children’s book about Decoy , which came out earlier this year. Unfortunately, Decoy’s appearance this year was not for another Ohtani MVP award. The Dodgers star saw his streak of three straight MVPs snapped this year as Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong won the award unanimously . Ohtani finished second after a frustrating season by his own admission. After a promising start to the season, Ohtani’s performances tailed off significantly, in part due to injury. He looked like a shell of himself by September and October as the Dodgers’ hopes of sealing a third successive World Series title came up short against the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS. Hopefully, an offseason’s worth of rest at home with Decoy can get Ohtani back to his best by the start of next season. item.title: Here's why Ja'Marr Chase says he loves late games, White Bengal
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase explained why he's looking forward to an NFL Week 10 showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium. "I think I love late games," Chase told reporters Nov. 12. "I get the whole day to sleep and get my rest up. I think that's the best part about the late games. Kick it with my kids and family for the half of the day. But I don't know, it's something about just playing at nighttime with the lights going. It feels like Friday night football when you're a kid again, you know?" "I just love the fact that it's like a high school football, you know?" Chase continued. "You get to play with the big lights on, and that was the big emphasis when I was in high school." Chase said it's important for the Bengals to be detail-oriented against Pittsburgh. "I think the guys have been realizing they've got to want it more," Chase said. "I think that's the biggest thing. We've got to want it more, especially when we're playing in tough games like this. And every play is going to count, you know what I'm saying? Even when you don't think the ball is coming or even a blocking scheme, whatever may happen, you've got to take that play seriously every play. And I think the guys have been cracking down on the smaller details and everything else to make us win." "I think at the end of the day, you've got to look at the game as it's the first game of the season," Chase continued. "You look at it as the first game of the season, and that's how we need to look at it. We don't need to look at it as AFC North, No. 1 seed. ... None of that should be in our head. It should be looking at it as 0-0, first game of the season. We've got to go out there and try to win." Chase was asked what he thinks when he sees the photo of him giving ex-Steeler Minkah Fitzpatrick the double bird . "I love it," Chase said. "Because I want to do it again, but I don't want to get fined. So I love it, though. But it's a cool picture, though. Honestly, it's really, really cool, though. ... Yeah, I would definitely do that again, yeah. ... I don't even know what made me do that, bro. I'll be honest." Chase said he looks forward to the White Bengal game. "Pretty cool," Chase said. "I think it's awesome. You know, I like – I actually like how the stadium looks when it's like this. You know what I'm saying? It looks a lot cooler. It looks a lot better. But I definitely can feel I have all the energy for the week. ... I think it's just good, man. A lot of the times the fans are like all – I'm not going to say they're all over, but everybody has their unique thing, what they do when it comes to the game. I think this is around the time when we get to see everybody on one color." Joe Burrow somehow hasn't played in a primetime time at home in the regular season against an AFC North opponent. item.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore ruled out for rest of 2026 season
item.description: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. Before the Illinois game, Moore told The Oregonian/OregonLive that he felt good but didn’t know if he’d return this season and was taking it “one day at a time.” “That’s all I can do,” he said. He then began throwing passes on the field in shorts and a sweatshirt. Saturday’s loss all but knocked Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) out of the national playoff picture and led Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: Dame Time is back in Portland — and the Blazers look dangerous
item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.title: Giants’ John Harbaugh Issues Strong Statement After Commanders Loss
item.description: The New York Giants appeared headed for another big divisional win on Thursday Night Football against the Washington Commanders. Unfortunately, disaster struck late and saw the team fall to their division rival by a final score of 24-21. Late in the fourth quarter, the Giants were stopped to a three-and-out with just 1:54 left in the game. After that, the New York defense allowed Washington to score on a three-play, 71-yard touchdown drive that took just 49 seconds off of the clock. On the final possession of the game, J.J. McCarthy threw an interception to Rasul Douglas with 34 seconds left that ended the game. With the loss, the Giants fell to 5-3-1 on the year. The Commanders, on the other hand, improved to 3-5-1. Needless to say, the defeat was a very disappointing finish to what had been a solid all-around game. New York did enough to be in a position to win. At the end of the day, the Giants simply didn’t finish. Following the game, head coach John Harbaugh spoke out with a strong statement about his team’s loss. Cowboys Hoping to Get Jaishawn Barham Going at Edge They broke down so fully this season that by last week against the Colts, Barham not only did not start, but he played just three snaps for the Cowboys. Furthermore, his potential as a solution at linebacker is, at least in the short term, taking a hit. Barham spent the past week adjusting to life on the outside, working with the edge rushers–a group that has been decimated by injuries to Donovan Ezeiruaku and Malachi Lawrence. Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker explained the thinking : “Next man up, we have some guys who have played significant steps throughout the year. That’s a rotational position by nature. So it’s not like guys are going to be coming out of nowhere to play. Then we’ll get Jaishawn more involved there. He’s kind of been involved there in some spotlight duty already with some different packages we’ve had throughout the season. We’ll be able to deploy him there some too.” It won’t be entirely new for Barham, even in the NFL. He has mostly played in the middle, but PFF does record him with 27 snaps on the edge, too. Barham is a hard-hitting defensive football player. But he needs a position. item.title: Wild Get Brutal Injury News During Maple Leafs Clash
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 24: Joel Eriksson Ek #14 and Quinn Hughes #43 of the Minnesota Wild talk during the second period Kraken at Climate Pledge Arena on October 24, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty The good news for the Minnesota Wild is that forward Matt Boldy registered a hat trick as part of Thursday’s contest against the Toronto Maple Leafs at Scotiabank Arena, while defenseman Quinn Hughes recorded his third-career point streak of 10+ games, joining rare NHL company. The bad news is that the Wild, who have already played the entire season without defenseman Brock Faber, lost one of their most important forwards during the contest. Following a collision with Jake McCabe, forward Joel Eriksson Ek departed and has not returned. Minnesota Wild Forward Joel Eriksson Ek Departs Clash Against Leafs With Injury Getty (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) During the second period of play, Eriksson Ek collided in the neutral zone with Toronto’s Jake McCabe and fell to the ice awkwardly. He also needed assistance making his way off the ice and down the tunnel toward the locker room. Joel Eriksson Ek collided with Jake McCabe and needed assistance getting off the ice 🤕 pic.twitter.com/iwOG1topXN — Gino Hard (@GinoHard_) November 13, 2026 So far, there has been no official update from the Wild about his condition, but the fact that he did not return to the third period has fans naturally concerned. Last season during the Stanley Cup Playoffs, Eriksson Ek suffered a broken hand in the deciding game against the rival Dallas Stars and missed the entire second round against the rival Colorado Avalanche. He’s played in 20 games so far this season, and has six goals with 11 assists for 17 points along with an impressive plus-15 rating. Eriksson Ek Is A Seasoned Wild Veteran Eriksson Ek made his NHL debut with the Wild, who took him in the first round (20th overall pick) in the 2016 NHL Draft, and scored in his first game. After bouncing between the Wild, the American Hockey League, and Sweden early in his career, he established himself as a regular NHL center. He broke out in 2020-21 after moving into a top-line role, scoring 19 goals before signing an eight-year, $42 million extension. He continued to improve, reaching 26 goals and 49 points in 2021-22 while becoming known as a strong two-way player and earning recognition as one of the NHL’s better defensive forwards. He reached 100 career goals in November 2023 after overcoming a fractured fibula that ended his 2022-23 season. He registered a career-high 30 goals in 2023-24, and followed that up with campaigns of 14 goals and 19 goals over the next two seasons; he was limited to just 46 games in 2024-25. item.title: Extra Effort: Metamora’s Addison Robison uses swimming to bring fun to students, could use it to serve country
item.description: METAMORA, Ill. (WMBD/WYZZ) -- Addie Robison's high school swim career comes to an end this week. She's sad to see it end. "I used to not enjoy it as much as I do now," said Robison on the eve of the state swim meet. "I feel making the friends I have in swimming, really helps me enjoy the sport so much more." And she's spreading that joy of swimming around central Illinois. The Metamora High School honor roll student teaches swim lessons and has for years. She says she teaches swimmers as young as two-years-old and she stresses enjoyment over performance. "Even before high school when I could have a job, I would teach swim lessons. I've loved it," said Robison. "Seeing the young kids grow and become better swimmers. Making sure they enjoy it. Enjoying it is the most important thing." On Nov. 19. Robison will be sworn into Coast Guard. After high school graduation, she'll head to an 8-week Boot Camp in New Jersey. She's hoping her ten years of swimming prepares her to be an Aviation Survival Technician, who performs high-risk search and rescue operations. "There's only one women in the entire Coast Guard that is an AST. It's physically demanding," Robison said. "I always thought it would be an amazing thing to do and will be rewarding." Her coach thinks she can do it. "Her dad is a military guy. They train together," said Metamora swim coach Shane Morrison. "Not just in competing but her work ethic, gives her an advantage, in my opinion." Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. All rights reserved.
